# IQV (IQVIA Holdings Inc.) — Technical Analysis Report
**Analysis date: 2026-10-09 | Verified close: $259.88**

## Indicator selection rationale
Selected indicators cover trend (close_50_sma, close_200_sma, close_10_ema), momentum (macd, macdh, rsi), volatility (boll_ub, atr, with boll/boll_lb from the verified snapshot). Together they frame a stock in a strong long-term uptrend undergoing a short-term pullback: the moving-average stack quantifies trend distance, MACD/histogram capture the momentum deceleration, RSI flags the neutralization of the prior overbought push, and Bollinger bands + ATR bound the current trading range and risk sizing.

## Trend structure
The long-term trend is unambiguously bullish. Price at $259.88 sits ~25.7% above the rising 200 SMA ($206.79) and ~1.2% above the 50 SMA ($256.86). Both averages are rising steadily — the 50 SMA gained roughly 24 points over the last 30 rows (232.77 → 256.86), and the 200 SMA has climbed every single session shown. The wide, expanding gap between the two averages confirms a mature, healthy uptrend.

The short-term picture is corrective. The 10 EMA ($262.23) has rolled over and price closed below it for the sixth consecutive session — the first sustained sub-10-EMA stretch in the data window. Price is pinned between the 50 SMA below ($256.86) and the 10 EMA above ($262.23), a classic consolidation-after-rally posture.

## Momentum
MACD is still positive (0.81) but has collapsed from 9.05 on 2026-09-09 — a >90% deceleration in one month. The MACD histogram has been negative since at least mid-September and deepened through early October (-2.31 on 10-07), though the last two readings (-2.27 → -2.10) show the very first signs of contraction. MACD crossed below its signal line (macds = 2.92) — a confirmed bearish crossover within an intact uptrend.

RSI at 47.93 has cooled from the mid-60s readings of mid-September and sits just below neutral. No bullish divergence is confirmed yet (price made marginal new lows vs. RSI), but momentum decay is decelerating, consistent with the histogram.

## Volatility and key levels
ATR is elevated at ~7.43 (~2.9% of price), stable-to-rising through the pullback — daily swings remain wide, so position sizing should assume ±$7-8 daily ranges. Price closed just above the lower Bollinger band at $256.09 (today's low $257.73 tagged that zone and was bought), while the upper band sits at $276.31 — close to the recent swing high zone around $275-277 (10-06 high $274.28, 9-24 close $275.02). The mid-band at $266.20 is the mean-reversion target overhead.

## Actionable read
- **Bull case:** Uptrend intact (price > rising 50/200 SMA), lower Bollinger band held on 10-08/10-09, histogram starting to contract. A reclaim of the 10 EMA (~$262) and then the mid-band (~$266) would signal the pullback is complete. Entries near $256-258 with a stop below ~$249 (50 SMA minus ~1 ATR) offer favorable structure.
- **Bear/risk case:** A decisive close below the 50 SMA ($256.86) and lower band ($256.09) on elevated volume would open a deeper correction toward prior congestion in the low-$240s. The negative MACD crossover and sub-10-EMA posture argue against aggressive adds until momentum confirms.
- **Watch:** MACD histogram turning positive, and whether the 50 SMA continues rising into a test.

# IQV (IQVIA Holdings Inc.) — Fundamental Analysis Report
**As of 2026-10-09 | All figures USD millions, SEC EDGAR filings as of that date**

## Company Profile
IQVIA Holdings Inc. (ticker: IQV) is a leading global provider of clinical research services (CRO), commercial insights, and healthcare intelligence to the life sciences industry. Formed from the 2016 Quintiles–IMS Health merger (visible in the balance sheet jump from ~$4.1B to ~$21B in total assets in late 2016), it operates two main engines: Technology & Analytics Solutions and Research & Development Solutions.

**Data caveat:** Point-in-time market cap, valuation multiples, and insider transactions were withheld by the vendor for this date; analysis below is built solely from filed financial statements.

## Revenue & Earnings Trend
Revenue has grown steadily and consistently:

| 2017 (post-merger) | ~$2,360–2,520 | Step-change from merger |
| 2019 | ~$2,684–2,895 | Organic growth |

Operating income has expanded from ~$300–495/qtr (2021–22) to $514–553/qtr in recent filings — operating margin ~12.5–13.5%.

## Balance Sheet

- **Investing:** mostly capex + periodic acquisitions (note -$1,529 9M-2021, -$1,391 9M-2023, -$1,201 9M-2025 — consistent bolt-on M&A appetite).
- **Financing:** net outflows recently (-$433 in latest 9M period), indicating debt paydown and/or buybacks rather than new issuance.

1. **Consistent compounding:** ~9 consecutive years of uninterrupted quarterly revenue growth post-merger; latest quarter is the highest ever (~$4.15B). No seasonality-driven red flags.
2. **Margin expansion:** operating margin improved from ~8% (2019–20) to ~13% — earnings growing faster than revenue.
3. **Cash-generative:** OCF ~$1.9B/yr against capex ~$0.55B — ~$1.3B+ annual FCF, funding buybacks/debt paydown.
4. **Leverage is the main risk:** liabilities ~$23.3B (likely ~$14B+ debt incl. in that figure) makes IQV sensitive to rate and refinancing conditions; negative working capital is structural, not acute.

Bull Analyst: # Bull Case: IQV (IQVIA Holdings Inc.) — Opening Argument

Let me make the case plainly: IQVIA is the dominant player in a structurally growing industry, it just posted the highest revenue quarter in its history, its margins are expanding, its cash generation is excellent — and the market is offering it to us at a discount, sitting on layered technical support after a healthy pullback. This is the kind of setup bulls should embrace, not fear.

## 1. A compounding machine, not a cyclical story

Nine consecutive years of uninterrupted quarterly revenue growth since the Quintiles–IMS merger. The latest filed quarter printed ~$4.15B — an all-time record. Operating margin has expanded from ~8% in 2019–20 to ~13% today, meaning earnings are compounding *faster* than the top line. This isn't a recovery story or a hope trade; it's a franchise executing at its best-ever level.

## 2. Capital-light cash engine funding returns

Operating cash flow is running ~$1.9B+/yr (Q1-2026 alone: $618M, +9% YoY) against capex of only ~$0.55B/yr. That's ~$1.3B+ in annual free cash flow from a business that doesn't need to build anything to grow. Financing outflows show the company is paying down debt and buying back stock rather than issuing — management is converting the P&L into per-share value directly.

## 3. Moat and market structure

IQVIA is the largest CRO on earth, with a data/analytics arm (Technology & Analytics Solutions) that competitors like Medpace, ICON, and Parexel simply cannot replicate — it monetizes the same clinical relationships twice. Pharma outsourcing penetration keeps rising, and post-COVID R&D normalization is behind us. Any easing in the rate environment is a double tailwind: cheaper biotech funding flows straight into CRO bookings, and lower discount rates lift IQV's long-duration contract revenue.

## 4. The technicals support the thesis — this is a pullback, not a top

- Price sits ~25.7% above a *rising* 200 SMA and just above a *rising* 50 SMA ($256.86). The long-term uptrend is unambiguous.
- The correction is controlled: price held the lower Bollinger band ($256.09) on 10-08 and 10-09 — buyers are defending the level.
- The MACD histogram just turned from -2.27 to -2.10 — the first contraction in weeks, i.e., the momentum decay is itself decelerating. RSI at 48 is neutral, giving plenty of room to run without being overbought.
- Reclaiming the 10 EMA (~$262) and mid-band (~$266) reopens the path to $275–277. Entry near $256–258 with a stop below ~$249 offers a favorable ~2:1+ risk/reward on structure alone.

## 5. Pre-empting the bear case

Yes, leverage is real — liabilities ~$23.3B against ~$6.2B equity, and negative working capital of ~$2.1B. But this is the *structural* post-merger capital structure of a services business carrying deferred revenue, not an acute deterioration: cash is up to ~$1.95B, equity is recovering, and net financing flows show deleveraging, not distress. The bear case requires a biotech funding collapse or a spike in rates — neither of which is evidenced in the data (and note the macro feeds returned *no contrary evidence*, not actual bad news).

On sentiment: the bears may cite "no retail interest." Zero StockTwits chatter is the normal baseline for an institutionally-owned mega-cap CRO — silence is not a signal. IQV trades on bookings, backlog, and earnings, not on cashtags.

## Bottom line

Record revenue, expanding margins, ~$1.3B+ FCF, a rising 50/200 SMA stack, support being defended at the lower band, and momentum decay flattening out. The bull case rests on verified financials and a technically intact uptrend; the bear case rests on macro conditions nobody in this dataset has actually confirmed. Accumulate near $256–258 with disciplined risk. The trend is your friend until the 50 SMA says otherwise.

Bear Analyst: # Bear Case: IQV (IQVIA Holdings Inc.) — Rebuttal

My bull colleague gave you a polished story: record revenue, rising SMAs, free cash flow. Let me tell you what he glossed over — because the difference between a good company and a good stock is exactly what he isn't pricing in.

## 1. "Record revenue" is doing the heavy lifting — look at the earnings underneath

He keeps repeating "highest revenue quarter in history." Fine. Now look at the earnings line he quoted and promptly walked past: diluted EPS went from $1.93 in Q1-2025 to $1.61 in the latest filed quarter. That's a ~17% year-over-year EPS *decline* at peak revenue. Revenue compounding while per-share earnings shrink means the growth is being bought — through bolt-on M&A (-$1.2B in investing outflows in the 9M-2025 period alone), through margin-squeezed contract wins, or through share count and cost dynamics the headline doesn't show. A "compounding machine" that compounds revenue but not EPS is a machine running harder to stand still. Nine years of revenue growth is real; so is the fact that the market pays for earnings, not for revenue records.

## 2. The leverage isn't "structural" — it's a loaded spring with an unknown rate backdrop

He calls ~$23.3B in liabilities against ~$6.2B in equity "the structural post-merger capital structure." That's a relabeling exercise, not an argument. Liabilities at ~78% of assets with negative working capital of ~$2.1B means IQV is a leveraged borrower whose equity cushion is thin — roughly $1 of equity for every $3.75 of liabilities. His defense rests entirely on rates cooperating. And what did the macro report actually establish? Nothing. FRED unavailable, no 10Y print, no Fed funds path, no rate-cut odds. He framed that as "no contrary evidence." That's backwards. The entire bull thesis on the balance sheet is conditional on an easing cycle that *nobody in this dataset has confirmed*. If the 10Y is drifting higher, IQV gets hit twice: refinancing costs on its own leveraged stack, and frozen biotech funding that starves its customer pipeline. "The data didn't disprove it" is not a foundation for a leveraged long-duration trade — it's an unpriced risk.

## 3. The technical picture is weaker than "healthy pullback" admits

Strip the adjectives and here's the tape: MACD collapsed from 9.05 to 0.81 in one month — a >90% momentum wipeout — with a confirmed bearish crossover below the signal line. Price has closed under the 10 EMA for six straight sessions, the first sustained stretch of that kind in the window. RSI went from mid-60s to sub-50. His evidence of stabilization is the histogram ticking from -2.27 to -2.10 — a single two-session contraction inside a deeply negative trend. That's noise dressed up as a turn. And his "support being defended" framing ignores the obvious: price is now *pinned* against the 50 SMA and lower Bollinger band at ~$256. Support that gets tested repeatedly tends to break. The report itself says a decisive close below $256 opens the low-$240s — a ~5-7% downside gap versus ~6% upside to $275-277 resistance. That's not a favorable asymmetry; it's a coin flip where the downside door just swung open.

## 4. The moat argument has a blind spot: the customer base is the risk

IQV's customers are biotechs and pharma — a funding-sensitive clientele. The CRO model's weakness isn't competition from ICON or Medpace; it's that IQV's bookings, backlog, and book-to-bill are derivatives of biotech funding conditions, and none of those metrics appear in this dataset at all. We're being asked to buy the dominant player in an industry whose demand signal — backlog — is literally unchecked. Meanwhile drug-pricing policy (IRA negotiation rounds) is a live, recurring headline risk the macro report flags as historically gap-inducing for IQV, and we have zero visibility into the current policy calendar.

## 5. What the silence actually means

He says zero retail chatter is normal for IQV. True — and irrelevant in his favor. What's not normal: *every* informational channel in this dataset went dark the same week. No news feed, no Reddit, no FRED, no Polymarket, no insider data, no backlog metrics. The bull wants you to accumulate into an information vacuum because the *cached fundamentals* looked good in March. When filings are the only thing you can see and the newest of them shows EPS down 17% YoY, "no bad news" isn't reassurance — it's the absence of a sell signal you can't actually verify.

## Bottom line

- EPS declining ~17% YoY at peak revenue — growth is being bought, not earned.
- ~78% liabilities-to-assets with negative working capital, and the easing cycle it's leveraged against is *unconfirmed*, not benign.
- MACD down >90% with a confirmed bearish crossover; price six sessions under the 10 EMA and pressed against the 50 SMA — the support he's praising is one bad session from becoming resistance at the low-$240s.
- The demand metrics that actually move IQV — backlog, book-to-bill, biotech funding — are absent from every report here.

The bull case requires a benign rate path, resilient biotech funding, and technical support to hold — none verified. The bear case requires only that one of those assumptions fail. Risk/reward at $259.88, pinned to support with deteriorating momentum, favors waiting for either a confirmed momentum reversal above $266 or a better price in the $240s — not accumulation at the edge of a trapdoor.
